skill.name: nft-standards
skill.description: Guide ERC-721 and ERC-1155 implementation, NFT metadata, royalties, soulbound tokens, dynamic NFTs, and gas-efficient minting.
skill.summary: Build and review NFT contracts using common token standards and metadata patterns.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All static alerts are false positives caused by Solidity require statements and Markdown backticks, with no host command execution present. Two example contracts contain genuine business logic risks involving unrestricted progression and soulbound token minting.

remediation.issue: Dynamic NFT owners can submit any experience amount.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict progression updates to an authorized game contract or verify signed updates with bounds and replay protection.

remediation.issue: Anyone can mint a soulbound token to any address.
remediation.suggestion: Add issuer authorization, recipient consent where appropriate, and explicit issuance policy checks before minting.

content.value_statement: NFT contracts require careful choices across token standards, metadata, royalties, and minting. This skill provides practical Solidity patterns and implementation guidance.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use ERC-721 or ERC-1155.
Provides Solidity examples for minting, burning, supply limits, and metadata.
Shows off-chain IPFS and on-chain metadata structures.
Demonstrates EIP-2981 royalty reporting and fee limits.
Covers soulbound, dynamic, and ERC721A contract patterns.
limitations: Examples are educational and require security review before deployment.
Some examples omit imports, helper functions, tests, and deployment configuration.
Library APIs may differ across OpenZeppelin and ERC721A versions.
The skill does not audit deployed contracts or verify marketplace behavior.

use_cases.title: Plan a Digital Art Collection
use_cases.description: Compare ERC-721 designs, metadata storage, supply limits, mint pricing, and royalty support.

use_cases.title: Model Multi-Token Game Items
use_cases.description: Design ERC-1155 item types, batch minting, burning, supply controls, and shared metadata.

use_cases.title: Review an NFT Architecture
use_cases.description: Check token standards, metadata choices, transfer rules, royalties, and gas optimization before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an NFT Standard
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare ERC-721 and ERC-1155 for [project]. Consider asset uniqueness, editions, batch transfers, metadata, and marketplace compatibility.

prompt_templates.title: Design Collection Metadata
prompt_templates.prompt: Design metadata for [collection] using [IPFS or on-chain storage]. Include traits, image handling, update policy, and marketplace compatibility.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Minting Contract
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an educational [ERC-721 or ERC-1155] contract for [requirements]. Include supply limits, access control, payments, events, and testing notes.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Advanced NFT Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this NFT design: [design]. Analyze authorization, supply accounting, metadata integrity, royalties, transfer restrictions, gas costs, and upgrade risks.

output_examples.input: Which standard fits a game with fungible potions and unique swords?
output_examples.output: Use ERC-1155 for shared item types and efficient batches. Use ERC-721 separately when every sword needs unique ownership and metadata.

output_examples.input: Review a soulbound achievement token design.
output: Define whether holders may burn tokens.
Block transfers while preserving mint and burn operations.
Document revocation, privacy, and recipient consent.

best_practices: Pin dependency versions and match examples to the selected library release.
Test authorization, supply boundaries, payment handling, metadata, and interface support.
Obtain an independent security review before deploying contracts that manage assets or payments.
anti_patterns: Do not deploy tutorial snippets without compilation, tests, and security review.
Do not allow public state updates when an authorized issuer or oracle should control them.
Do not rely on marketplace royalty enforcement without documenting its limitations.

faq.question: When should I use ERC-721?
faq.answer: Use ERC-721 when each token is individually owned and needs a unique identifier or metadata record.

faq.question: When should I use ERC-1155?
faq.answer: Use ERC-1155 for multiple token types, editions, fungible items, or efficient batch transfers.

faq.question: Does this skill produce deployment-ready contracts?
faq.answer: No. The examples require dependency alignment, compilation, tests, threat modeling, and independent security review.

faq.question: Can metadata be stored on-chain?
faq.answer: Yes. On-chain metadata improves availability but increases gas costs and requires careful encoding.

faq.question: Are EIP-2981 royalties guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. EIP-2981 reports royalty information, but marketplaces decide whether to pay or enforce royalties.

faq.question: Can this skill audit an existing contract?
faq.answer: It can support structured review, but it does not replace automated tests, specialist audits, or deployed contract analysis.
